components.css: :host{--bg:#F3F4F6;--surface:#FFFFFF;--sunk:#F1F2F5;--ink:#15171C;--muted:#687080;--line:#E2E4E9;--accent:#3355FF;--accent-ink:#FFFFFF;--accent-soft:#E9EDFF;--play:#F28A1B;--play-soft:#FFF1E2;--t-dia:#8A93A6;--t-bor:#8B5CF6;--t-sec:#EA6A2A;--t-chr:#E0457B;--t-jazz:#10A38C} .ds-seg{display:inline-flex;gap:2px;background:var(--sunk);border-radius:10px;padding:3px}.ds-seg button{font-family:Geist,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,-apple-system,sans-serif;border:0;background:none;border-radius:8px;padding:7px 12px;font-weight:600;font-size:13.5px;color:var(--muted);cursor:pointer}.ds-seg button:hover{color:var(--ink)}.ds-seg button[aria-selected=true]{background:var(--surface);color:var(--ink);box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / .1),0 0 0 1px var(--line)}.ds-seg button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:2px}

components.css: :host{--bg:#F3F4F6;--surface:#FFFFFF;--sunk:#F1F2F5;--ink:#15171C;--muted:#687080;--line:#E2E4E9;--accent:#3355FF;--accent-ink:#FFFFFF;--accent-soft:#E9EDFF;--play:#F28A1B;--play-soft:#FFF1E2;--t-dia:#8A93A6;--t-bor:#8B5CF6;--t-sec:#EA6A2A;--t-chr:#E0457B;--t-jazz:#10A38C} .ds-track{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,minmax(0,1fr));gap:6px;background:var(--sunk);border-radius:14px;padding:12px}.ds-clip{font-family:Geist,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,-apple-system,sans-serif;position:relative;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;color:var(--ink);border:1px solid color-mix(in srgb,var(--k) 28%,transparent);border-radius:10px;background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--k) 11%,var(--surface));box-shadow:inset 3px 0 0 var(--k);padding:5px 10px 6px 13px;min-height:62px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;transition:background .15s,box-shadow .15s,border-color .15s}.ds-clip:hover{background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--k) 18%,var(--surface))}.ds-clip b{font-weight:600;font-size:21px;line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.02em}.ds-clip span{font-size:12px;font-weight:500;color:var(--muted)}.ds-clip i{position:absolute;right:10px;top:6px;font:normal 10px 'Geist Mono',ui-monospace,monospace;color:var(--muted)}.ds-sel{border-color:var(--accent);box-shadow:inset 3px 0 0 var(--k),0 0 0 2px var(--accent)}.ds-playing{background:var(--play-soft);border-color:var(--play);box-shadow:inset 3px 0 0 var(--play),0 0 0 2px var(--play),0 0 24px -4px color-mix(in srgb,var(--play) 60%,transparent)}.ds-clip:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:2px}.ds-k-dia{--k:var(--t-dia)}.ds-k-bor{--k:var(--t-bor)}.ds-k-sec{--k:var(--t-sec)}.ds-k-chr{--k:var(--t-chr)}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-clip{transition:none}}

narrative.overview:
Chord Changes should feel like a calm, well-lit workbench next to the instrument. The chart is the page you're working on. It sits in the middle, on the brightest paper, with the most lift. Tools are laid out within reach on either side: Create on the left, the selected chord and its swap ideas on the right, the Play bar pinned along the front edge. Nothing on the desk is showy. The desk is grey, the paper is white, and colour belongs to the music.

The tone is friendly and approachable. Pill-shaped chips for moods and genres, generous rounded corners, a soft cobalt wash behind the one-tap card in Simple view and plain-language hints in muted grey all tell a newcomer they can't break anything. Beneath that warmth there's a quiet precision: tabular figures, mono bar numbers, beats snapped to a grid. It's still a real tool for working songwriters. Density stays moderate. Advanced adds more tools, but never makes them smaller or heavier.

It is deliberately **not a toy** (no cartoon, gamified or kid-app styling, even in Simple view), **not a DAW clone** (no dark, dense, knob-heavy pro-audio skin), and **not a theory textbook** (no notation-first, academic presentation; theory appears as plain words and colour).
keyCharacteristics: Neutral grey desk, white paper surfaces, colour reserved for meaning
Chords drawn as tinted clips on a timeline, coloured by harmonic function
Cobalt means "selected or act", amber means "playing now", and nothing else uses them
One typeface (Geist) for everything, with Geist Mono for small numbers
Soft rounded forms and pill chips; one ambient lift, on the chart alone
Full light and dark themes, following the system with a manual override

rules.name: The Colour Means Something Rule
rules.body: A colour on screen is harmonic function, selection, or playback. Don't use any of them as decoration.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is "selected or act". Amber is "sounding now". When a clip is both selected and playing, amber wins.

rules.name: The Quiet Majority Rule
rules.body: In-key chords are tinted slate, not a brand colour. Most of the chart should look calm, so that borrowed, secondary and chromatic chords stand out as the interesting moments.

rules.name: The Weight Not Face Rule
rules.body: Build hierarchy with Geist's weights and sizes. Don't add a second typeface.

rules.name: The Chord Is The Headline Rule
rules.body: Chord names are always the heaviest, tightest-tracked text in their context. Their Roman numeral or function sits beside or below in Graphite.

rules.name: The One Lifted Page Rule
rules.body: Only the chart card carries the ambient lift. Other panels sit flat on the desk with a hairline border.

dos: Do keep colour for meaning: function tints on chords, Cobalt for selection or action, amber for playback.
Do put the chart on the brightest, most lifted surface. It's the page on the desk.
Do use pills for choices a beginner taps (moods, genres, families) and rounded rectangles for tools.
Do build hierarchy with Geist weights 400, 500 and 600 and tight tracking on chord names. Use Geist Mono only for small numbers and the text chart.
Do give every new chord-related element its function colour through the shared `--k` variable (`.k-dia`, `.k-bor`, `.k-sec`, `.k-chr`, `.k-jazz`).
Do design every surface for both light and dark themes using the existing tokens, and check it at phone, tablet and desktop widths.
Do keep transitions short (150–200ms) and only when reduced motion is off.
donts: Don't make it a toy: no cartoon illustrations, mascots, confetti, badges or gamified chrome, even in Simple view.
Don't make it a DAW clone: no dark-by-default pro-audio skin, knobs, meters or dense rack layouts.
Don't make it a theory textbook: don't lead with staff notation or academic labels. Show function as colour and plain words first.
Don't use Cobalt or amber decoratively, and don't introduce a new hue unless it maps to a new harmonic category.
Don't give ambient shadows to panels other than the chart card. Stay flat on the desk.
